messages:
maria: Heads-up — on the int8 quant bringup I hit an early streaming cutoff for a chat model. Looks like chat templates that mix different EOS sentinels are triggering it.
priya: repro steps?
maria: Converted HF checkpoint -> redwood format with our convert script, kept tokenizer as-is. When streaming, responses stop immediately after a short chunk and client gets an empty final message. Happens intermittently but reproducible with the toy prompt in the repro.
sam: any logs from the runtime?
maria: runtime log snippet:
```
[2026-03-19 13:04:12.312] stream: recv tokens 120..130
[2026-03-19 13:04:12.313] stream: detected eos token id=50256 at pos=128
[2026-03-19 13:04:12.314] stream: flush and close stream (reason=EOS)
[2026-03-19 13:04:12.315] stream: received token id=50256 at pos=129 (duplicate)
```
maria: note the duplicate eos id right after close, and sometimes the client already saw a truncated output.
bryan: do we know which sentinel the tokenizer actually uses? Some HF models use "</s>" others use "" and chat templates sometimes append a stop token too.
priya: quick check command to confirm tokenizer and config alignment:
```bash
python - <<PY
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('our-local-copy')
print('eos_token:', repr(t.eos_token))
print('eos_token_id:', t.eos_token_id)
PY
```
priya: also inspect config.json for "eos_token_id" — we had a few converted packages where config.eos_token_id was left as -1 or pointed at a different id.
maria: confirmed mismatch on one package: tokenizer.eos_token_id was 50256 but config.json had eos_token_id: 1. That caused the runtime to match the wrong sentinel sometimes, then later the tokenizer emitted the real eos and we double-detected.
sam: aha. But why the streaming close happens so fast? Could chunk boundaries be splitting a multi-byte sentinel so the matcher fires on a partial pattern?
bryan: another wrinkle: chat templates we use for system+user sometimes inject explicit stop markers (we append "</s>" for historical reasons) AND the model has "" mapped — conversion ended up keeping both in text and special tokens, so output can contain two distinct EOS tokens back-to-back. Streaming runtime currently treats any matched EOS token as immediate termination.
priya: workaround ideas: (1) conversion step should canonicalize sentinels — map all known variants ("</s>", "", "<|endoftext|>") to tokenizer.eos_token and set config.eos_token_id = tokenizer.eos_token_id before saving; (2) streaming matcher should collapse consecutive EOS tokens (ignore duplicates within a 2-token window) and prefer matching the longest canonical sequence.
maria: here's a minimal conversion patch I tested locally:
```python
# after loading tokenizer & config during convert
if tokenizer.eos_token is None and tokenizer.special_tokens_map.get('eos_token'):
    tokenizer.eos_token = tokenizer.special_tokens_map['eos_token']
# normalize alternate strings to canonical eos
alt_eos = ['</s>', '', '<|endoftext|>']
for tok in alt_eos:
    if tok in tokenizer.get_vocab() and tok != tokenizer.eos_token:
        # merge token -> eos
        tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token': tok})
# force config to match tokenizer
config['eos_token_id'] = tokenizer.eos_token_id
# save
tokenizer.save_pretrained(outdir)
with open(os.path.join(outdir, 'config.json'), 'w') as f:
    json.dump(config, f)
```
priya: unit tests I added: generate sequences with template that appends both variants and assert streaming doesn't close until canonical eos seen; added quantized int8 job to CI.
sam: good. Also file a runtime issue: streaming matcher should not close mid-chunk if subsequent token bytes arrive in same network frame — treat immediate duplicate eos as likely noise and wait up to N ms or until next non-eos token. We can make this config flaggable.
bryan: agree. I'll open a PR with two parts: conversion normalization + streaming matcher tolerance. I'll link the repro and logs.
qa-bot: added test: eng-ml/eos-normalization.test -> CI matrix runs int8,int4,fp16.
maria: thanks — marking as blocked on PRs. Leaving the repro snippet in /tmp/eos_repro_<id>.json for whoever picks it up. :thumbsup:
